g1.label: 1. local varieties selected over generations are called ___
g1.why: Paragraph A: “local varieties, known as landraces, which had been selected over many generations” — one word, copied exactly.

g2.label: 2. a modern variety that fails when a new ___ appears
g2.why: Paragraph A: “A modern variety that fails when a new pest arrives” — “appears” paraphrases “arrives”.

g3.label: 3. drying and cooling slows down the ___ that make them age
g3.why: Paragraph B: drying and cooling “slow down the chemical processes of ageing”; “chemical processes of ageing” is four words and breaks the limit.

g4.label: 4. staff check samples by attempting to ___ some seeds
g4.why: Paragraph B: staff test each sample “by trying to germinate a few of its seeds” — the gap after “to” needs a verb.

g5.label: 5. the staff refused to eat the seeds, and ___ of them died
g5.why: Paragraph C: “they refused to eat them, and several died of hunger”.

g6.label: 6. seeds are stored at minus ___ degrees Celsius
g6.why: Paragraph D: seeds “are kept at minus 18 degrees Celsius” — a number is allowed by the instruction.

g7.label: 7. after a mild winter in 2017, ___ got into the tunnel
g7.why: Paragraph E: “In 2017, after an unusually warm Arctic winter, meltwater entered the entrance tunnel”.

g8.label: 8. the vault holds ___ copies of samples
g8.why: Paragraph D: other gene banks “send duplicate copies of their samples”; “original” is wrong because the originals stay with the depositors.

g9.label: 9. a centre forced out of Syria by ___
g9.why: Paragraph E: “the civil war had forced the centre to move its work” — a war is a conflict; “flooding” is the 2017 problem at the vault.

g10.label: 10. oak and cocoa seeds cannot survive being ___
g10.why: Paragraph F: recalcitrant seeds, such as oak and cocoa, “die if they are dried”.

g11.label: 11. a technique that is still ___ in its results
g11.why: Paragraph F: cryopreservation “has to be worked out species by species and success remains uneven” — uneven results are inconsistent.

g12.label: 12. frozen seeds cannot ___ as conditions change
g12.why: Paragraph F: critics argue “a seed held in a freezer stops adapting”.

g13.label: 13. experts regard field growing and storage as ___ approaches
g13.why: Paragraph F: specialists see the two approaches “as complements rather than rivals” — so “competing” says the opposite.

g1.label: 1. it holds ___ copies (gap 8)
g1.why: The gap comes before the noun “copies”, so it needs a word that describes it: an adjective.

g2.label: 2. forced out of Syria by ___ (gap 9)
g2.why: After the preposition “by” comes a noun: the thing that forced the centre out.

g3.label: 3. cannot survive being ___ (gap 10)
g3.why: After “being” comes a past participle, as in “being dried” — a verb form.

g4.label: 4. a technique that is still ___ (gap 11)
g4.why: After “is still” and before “in its results”, the gap describes the technique: an adjective.

g5.label: 5. frozen seeds cannot ___ (gap 12)
g5.why: After the modal “cannot” comes the base form of a verb.

g6.label: 6. regard them as ___ approaches (gap 13)
g6.why: The gap comes before the noun “approaches”, so it needs an adjective.

g1.label: 1. seeds are dried and sealed in ___
g1.why: Paragraph B: “sealed in airtight packets” — two words; “airtight packets and stored” is over the limit, and “airtight” alone leaves the sentence without a noun.

g2.label: 2. some species produce ___ seeds
g2.why: Paragraph F: “recalcitrant seeds” — the sentence already has “seeds”, so the gap takes one word; “what are known as recalcitrant” is over the limit.

g3.label: 3. each gene bank sends the vault ___ of its samples
g3.why: Paragraph D: “duplicate copies of their samples” — the gap needs a noun after “sends the vault”, and the full phrase is over the limit.

g4.label: 4. seeds kept in a freezer stop ___
g4.why: Paragraph F: a frozen seed “stops adapting”; “stop evolve” breaks the grammar, and “evolve alongside new pests” is four words.

g5.label: 5. regeneration is both slow and ___
g5.why: Paragraph B: regeneration “is slow and costly”; “slow and costly” repeats “slow and” and is over the limit, and “a process” does not fit after “slow and”.

g6.label: 6. was announced in 2014 → was completed in 2014 (review)
g6.why: An announcement says something will happen, not that it did — recalled from ielts-reading-true-false-not-given.html (Ex B).

g7.label: 7. a heading that repeats one detail (review)
g7.why: Headings that only echo a detail are the traps — recalled from ielts-reading-matching-headings.html (Ex C).
